newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says killed 26 Kurdish rebels in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says killed 26 Kurdish rebels in clashes.

text.p: Government forces have killed 26 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas in recent clashes in the southeast of Turkey, security officials said on Monday.
The emergency rule governor's office in the city of Diyarbakir said in a statement that the rebels had died in fighting in the provinces of Sirnak, Van, Diyarbakir and Siirt.

It did not specify when the clashes took place and did not refer to any Turkish casualties. But a military official told Reuters that two Turkish soldiers were killed in recent clashes in Hakkari province, near the border with Iraq.
Security officials said on Sunday that up to 20,000 troops, backed by helicopters, had joined land and air operations against PKK rebels in the east of the country.

The rebels ambushed a Turkish unit and killed nine soldiers at the weekend after PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan announced he would step up attacks in response to Turkey's bid to form a 10-km (six-mile) deep security zone inside northern Iraq to root out the PKK presence there.
More than 20,000 people have died in the rebels' 12-year-old fight for autonomy or independence in southeast Turkey.
